title: Matrix multiplication
summary: A row-major 2×3 matrix multiplies a 3×2 matrix. Each CUDA thread owns one output cell and reduces over the shared dimension.
example:
import numpy as np

left = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]], dtype=np.float32)
right = np.array([[7, 8], [9, 10], [11, 12]], dtype=np.float32)
product = np.matmul(left, right)
limitations: Fixed fixture uses two-dimensional row-major operands with shapes (2,3) and (3,2); batched broadcasting and other dtypes are not modeled.
The CUDA illustration uses one scalar accumulator per output and does not model NumPy dispatch, BLAS selection, tiling, or performance.

stages.title: Assign one output cell per thread
stages.summary: Flatten output coordinates into a thread index, then recover row and column.
stages.insight: Distinct output cells are independent and require no inter-thread reduction.

stages.title: Reduce over the shared dimension
stages.summary: Accumulate three matching left-row and right-column elements.
stages.insight: The inner dimension is the left matrix width and the right matrix height.

kernel.name: matmul_2x3_3x2
